label: copy-phase update gate keyed on fed-back token (t, p, y, ...)
predicate: (phase == 2) & (recall_idx >= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok("t"), tok("p"), tok("y"), tok("g"), tok("o"), tok("k"), tok("q"), tok("e"), 28])
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during original tokens or on <DEL>, and only on a re-seen token (in_first=0 always). Within the copy phase it is mostly off at recall_idx 1, more frequent at recall_idx 2-5 and on the last two outputs, and much more frequent for L=3-4. Rate depends strongly on which token is fed back as input: t (24% rate), p, y are highest, then g, o, k, q, e, digit 2. The strongest activations are on a fed-back t or p in short (L=3) sequences, e.g. "q t 3 <DEL> q [t]". The activation is distributed over many tokens and positions, so a token-set-by-copy-phase predicate gets only about 0.43 F1 / 0.72 mass recall on dev. It is not a clean single-concept unit.
